criteria.evidence: I read ci.yml line 400-401: `ci:` then `    name: fmt, clippy, tests`, still followed by `needs: [gate, fmt, clippy, test]` and `if: always()`. A Grep for job names in ci.yml shows that name only at line 401. Every other job keeps its own name (gate, fmt, clippy, test (shard ..), pass, history, attribution, pr-head). The workflow-level `name: ci` at line 37 is unchanged.

criteria.criterion: xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs contains a test that parses ci.yml and asserts that exactly one job is named `fmt, clippy, tests` and that its `needs` lists every check job (gate, fmt, clippy, test); it would fail on the previous file, where the final job is named `ci`. The old `name: ci` assertion in check_jobs is replaced.
criteria.evidence: I read the new code. `check_required_name` uses `jobs()` on the real ci.yml, requires exactly one job with the line `    name: fmt, clippy, tests`, requires that job to be `ci`, and requires its needs to include gate, fmt, clippy and test. The test `workflow_required_check_name_is_on_exactly_one_job_that_needs_every_check` passes. Its first mutation turns the name back into `    name: ci`, which rebuilds the base file exactly (the ci.yml diff is that one line), and the test asserts this is rejected. So the unwrap on the real file would fail against the base. In check_jobs, the old `name: ci` check is replaced by a call to `check_required_name(text)?`.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`: the new test and all existing ci_shards and policy tests pass, including the mutation tests that drop `if: always()` or a need.
criteria.evidence: I ran it. ci_shards: 19 passed, including workflow_jobs_reject_a_missing_gate_condition_need_or_timeout, workflow_jobs_are_separate_sharded_and_gated_by_ci and the new test. policy: 12 passed. fingerprint: 10 passed. The other xtask targets also passed, with 0 failures overall.

findings.summary: The name check matches only one exact line, so a quoted duplicate name would get past it.
findings.evidence: The filter is `lines.contains("    name: fmt, clippy, tests")`. This matches how the rest of ci_shards.rs parses the file and does not affect the real file today. Stripping YAML quotes before comparing, or using a YAML parser, would close the gap.

summary: This change does what was asked. In ci.yml, the final job (id `ci`) now has the display name `fmt, clippy, tests`, the check name that branch protection requires. The diff of ci.yml is that one line: the job id, `needs: [gate, fmt, clippy, test]`, `if: always()`, the steps and every other job are unchanged. xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs has a new helper, `check_required_name`, and a test that reads the real ci.yml. The test requires exactly one job to carry that name, requires that job to be `ci`, and requires it to need gate, fmt, clippy and test. It also confirms that three altered copies of the file are rejected: one with the name set back to `ci`, one with the name copied onto `pass`, and one with `fmt` dropped from needs. The first of these is exactly the base file, so the test would fail against the base. check_jobs now calls the helper instead of checking for `name: ci`. CHANGELOG.md amends the 0rz6 entry (the name, no change to branch protection needed, the EARLY_RUN_JOB mismatch marked resolved) and adds a Fixed entry that cites PR #314's HTTP 405. docs/design/ci-routing.md is updated to match. All changed files are on the deliverables list. I ran `cargo test -p xtask` (all pass), the new test on its own, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`, and all were clean. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs on this tree also passed. The only findings are small: the name check would miss a quoted duplicate name, and a header comment in ci.yml is slightly stale.
